To answer this question, we need to consider average height data by country or region.

- Americans are generally taller than Mexicans and Indians. Mexico and India have lower average heights compared to the US.
- Americans are not taller than the Dutch or the Netherlands; the Dutch are among the tallest people in the world.
- Finland and Scandinavia (which includes Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark) have average heights comparable to or slightly less than Americans, but generally, Americans are not taller than Scandinavians.
- Americans are not taller than Canadians; Canadians have similar or slightly taller average heights.
- Americans are not taller than Europeans in general; many European countries have average heights similar to or taller than Americans.
- The UK average height is slightly less than Americans, so Americans are taller than the UK on average.

From the options:

A. Americans are taller than Canadians. — No, Canadians are about the same or taller.
B. Americans are taller on average than Mexicans and Indians. — Yes, this is true.
C. The Dutch. — No, Dutch are taller.
D. Finland. — No, Finnish are about the same or taller.
E. The Netherlands. — No, same as Dutch.
F. Americans are taller on average than the Dutch. — No.
G. UK. — Yes, Americans are slightly taller on average than the UK.
H. People in the US are on average taller than Europeans. — No, many Europeans are taller.
I. Americans are taller than Scandinavians. — No.

Therefore, the correct options are B and G.

Since the question asks "Americans are taller on average than which other places?" and the options are single letters, the best answer is B (Mexicans and Indians) and G (UK). But since only one answer is expected, and B is more comprehensive and accurate, I will select B.

Answer: B
